front: What makes air brakes work?
back: Squeezed (compressed) air.
why: Air is the power, so you must keep enough of it.

front: Air brakes are really how many brake systems?
back: 3: service, parking, and emergency.
why: Think S-P-E: Stop, Park, Emergency.

front: What does the air compressor do?
back: Pumps air into the air tanks.

front: What does the governor control?
back: When the compressor pumps air into the tanks.

front: About what is the governor cut-out pressure?
back: About 125 psi.
why: Cut-out means the compressor stops pumping.

front: About what is the governor cut-in pressure?
back: About 100 psi.
why: Cut-in means the compressor starts pumping again.

front: If the compressor quits, can you still brake?
back: Yes, a few times, with air in the tanks.

front: Why do you drain the air tanks?
back: To get rid of water and oil.
why: Water can freeze in cold weather and make brakes fail.

front: What are the 2 kinds of tank drains?
back: Manual and automatic.

front: How often do you drain manual air tanks?
back: At the end of each driving day.
why: Drain them all the way.

front: What does an alcohol evaporator do?
back: Puts alcohol in the air to stop ice.
why: Ice in the valves can make brakes stop working.

front: In cold weather, how often do you fill the alcohol?
back: Check and fill it every day.

front: Where is the safety valve?
back: In the first tank the compressor fills.

front: What does the safety valve do?
back: Lets out air if pressure gets too high.
why: It guards the tanks from too much pressure.

front: At what pressure does the safety valve usually open?
back: 150 psi.

front: The safety valve lets out air. What should you do?
back: Have a mechanic fix the problem.
why: It means something is wrong.

front: What are other names for the brake pedal?
back: Foot valve or treadle valve.

front: What happens when you push the brake pedal harder?
back: More air pressure goes to the brakes.

front: Why not pump the brake pedal for no reason?
back: It lets air out faster than it refills.
why: If air gets too low, the brakes won't work.

front: What are foundation brakes?
back: The brakes at each wheel.

front: What is the most common foundation brake?
back: The S-cam drum brake.

front: What does the S-cam do to the brake shoes?
back: Spreads them apart, against the drum.

front: What does air in the brake chamber push?
back: A push rod, which moves the slack adjuster.
why: Order: chamber, push rod, slack adjuster, cam, shoes.

front: What does the supply pressure gauge show?
back: How much air is in the tanks.

front: What does the application pressure gauge show?
back: Air pressure you are putting on the brakes.

front: You need more brake pressure to keep the same speed. Why?
back: The brakes are fading.
why: Slow down and use a lower gear.

front: Low air warning must come on before what psi?
back: Before tank air falls below 55 psi.
why: Not 60. Older study sets get this wrong.

front: What is a wig wag?
back: An arm that drops into view when air is low.
why: It drops below 55 psi.

front: What turns on the brake lights in an air system?
back: The stop light switch, worked by air pressure.

front: Front brake limiting valve on slippery: what happens?
back: Air to the front brakes is cut in half.

front: Where should the front brake control be set?
back: On normal.
why: Front brakes are good in all conditions, even on ice.

front: Why are parking and emergency brakes held on by force, not air?
back: Air can leak away over time.
why: Spring brakes use strong springs.

front: While driving, what holds the spring brakes off?
back: Air pressure.
why: Lose the air, and the springs put the brakes on.

front: At what psi do truck spring brakes come fully on?
back: 20 to 45 psi (usually 20 to 30).

front: Low air light and buzzer come on. What do you do?
back: Stop safely right away.
why: Don't wait for the spring brakes to grab.

front: On newer trucks, what does the parking brake knob look like?
back: A yellow diamond-shaped push-pull knob.

front: How do you set the parking brake with the knob?
back: Pull it out. Push it in to release.

front: Should you push the brake pedal with spring brakes on?
back: No. It can damage the brakes.
why: Spring force plus air force is too much.

front: What does a modulating control valve do?
back: Puts the spring brakes on a little at a time.
why: You can use it if the service brakes fail.

front: Air brake tractors need ABS if built on or after when?
back: March 1, 1997.

front: Other air brake trucks, buses, trailers need ABS if built when?
back: On or after March 1, 1998.

front: Does ABS make your stopping distance shorter?
back: Not always. It helps you keep control.

front: What is a dual air brake system?
back: 2 separate air systems, 1 set of controls.
why: Each half has its own tanks and lines.

front: Dual system: how much air before you drive?
back: At least 100 psi in both systems.

front: One half of a dual system is very low. What happens?
back: Front or rear brakes are weak. Stops take longer.
why: Stop safely and get it fixed.

front: Before checking slack adjusters, what do you do?
back: Park level, chock wheels, release parking brakes.

front: A slack adjuster moves how far before it needs adjusting?
back: More than about 1 inch.
why: Measure where the push rod hooks on. Pull hard, wear gloves.

front: What is the most common problem at roadside checks?
back: Brakes out of adjustment.

front: Automatic slack adjuster is out of adjustment. What do you do?
back: Get it to a repair shop soon.
why: Fixing it by hand hides a real problem.

front: How do you test governor cut-out?
back: Fast idle. Gauge should stop rising near 125 psi.

front: How do you test governor cut-in?
back: Pump the pedal. Air should rise again near 100 psi.

front: Leak test, brakes released: max loss for a single vehicle?
back: Less than 2 psi in 1 minute.
why: Engine off, parking brake released.

front: Leak test, brakes released: max loss for a combination?
back: Less than 3 psi in 1 minute.

front: Leak test, pedal held down: max loss for a single vehicle?
back: 3 psi in 1 minute.
why: Engine off, hold the foot brake 1 minute.

front: Leak test, pedal held down: max loss for a combination?
back: 4 psi in 1 minute.
why: Memory hook: held = 3 and 4; released = 2 and 3.

front: Air leaks faster than allowed. What do you do?
back: Find and fix leaks before driving.

front: How do you test the low air warning?
back: Engine off, key on, pump the pedal.
why: It must come on before 55 psi.

front: How do you check spring brakes come on by themselves?
back: Keep pumping the pedal to lower the air.
why: Parking brake knob should pop out at 20 to 45 psi.

front: Dual system build-up: 85 to 100 psi takes how long?
back: Within 45 seconds.
why: Engine at working rpm.

front: Old single system build-up: 50 to 90 psi takes how long?
back: Within 3 minutes.
why: Engine idling at 600 to 900 rpm.

front: How fast do you go to test the service brakes?
back: About 5 mph, then brake firmly.
why: Feel for pulling to one side or slow stops.

front: Only the tractor has ABS. Trailer swings out. What do you do?
back: Let up on the brakes, if safe.

front: How do you brake a rig with ABS?
back: The same as always. Use only what you need.

front: Your ABS breaks. Do you still have brakes?
back: Yes, normal brakes still work.
why: Drive normally and get it fixed soon.

front: What is controlled braking?
back: Brake as hard as you can without locking wheels.
why: Keep steering moves very small.

front: What is stab braking?
back: Brake fully, let off when wheels lock, repeat.

front: Stab braking: how long until wheels roll again?
back: Up to 1 second.
why: Brake again too soon and the truck won't straighten.

front: What is brake lag?
back: Time for air to reach the brakes.
why: About half a second or more.

front: What 4 parts make up air brake stopping distance?
back: Perception, reaction, brake lag, braking distance.
why: Hook: See, React, Lag, Brake.

front: At 55 mph, how much distance does brake lag add?
back: About 32 feet.

front: At 55 mph, total stopping distance with air brakes?
back: Over 450 feet.

front: What causes brake fade?
back: Too much heat from using the brakes too much.
why: Use engine braking to save your brakes.

front: Some brakes are out of adjustment. What happens?
back: Other brakes overheat and fade.
why: Every brake must do its share. Check adjustment often.

front: On a long downhill, what slows you most?
back: The engine, in a low gear.
why: Brakes only help the engine.

front: Downhill: brake until you are how far below safe speed?
back: About 5 mph below safe speed.
why: Example: safe speed 40, brake down to 35, let off.

front: Low air: why stop before spring brakes come on?
back: Spring brakes may skid or take long to stop.
why: They don't work on all axles.

front: When should you not use the parking brakes?
back: When brakes are very hot, or wet and freezing.
why: Hot brakes get damaged. Wet brakes can freeze.

front: Leaving the truck for just a minute: set parking brake?
back: Yes. Always set brakes or chock wheels.
why: The truck could roll away.

front: What is a slack adjuster?
back: The arm the push rod moves to twist the S-cam.
why: Push rod, then slack adjuster, then cam, then shoes.

front: Must every air brake truck have a low air warning?
back: Yes. It is required.
why: It must come on before 55 psi.

front: Do front brakes make you skid on slick roads?
back: No. Front brakes work well in all conditions.
why: Front wheel skids are unlikely, even on ice.

front: What are spring brakes?
back: Springs that put on the brakes when air is gone.
why: Air holds the springs back while you drive.

front: How do you know a truck has ABS?
back: A yellow ABS lamp on the dash.
why: Trailers have a yellow lamp on the left side.

front: Belt-driven air compressor: what do you check?
back: That the belt is tight and in good shape.

front: Do automatic slack adjusters need checking?
back: Yes. Check them on every inspection.
why: All trucks built since 1994 have them.

front: How long can a brake drum crack be?
back: No longer than half the width of the friction area.

front: Name 2 bad signs on brake linings.
back: Soaked with oil or grease, or too thin.
why: Loose linings are bad, too.

front: Why be in a low gear before a long downhill?
back: The engine brakes so your brakes stay cool.
why: You can't downshift once speed builds.

front: Downhill braking: how long does each brake press last?
back: About 3 seconds.
why: Brake to 5 mph under safe speed, then let go.
